en.headline: Government to release Wang Fuk Court fire report and outline bid-rigging reforms on Thursday
en.dek: Sources say Chief Executive John Lee will announce criminal penalties for bid-rigging and other measures at a press conference as the independent committee's findings are made public.
body: The government is expected to release on Thursday the findings of an independent committee that investigated last November's fire at Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po, which killed 168 people, sources told local media.

Chief Executive John Lee and senior officials are due to hold a press conference on Thursday to outline a series of reforms, including legislation that would make bid-rigging in building maintenance works a criminal offence, according to the sources. Further briefings are planned for Friday.

Authorities also plan to set up a steering committee led by the Chief Secretary for Administration to oversee implementation of the recommendations and related legislative changes. The government is expected to propose amendments to the Buildings Ordinance that would shift from industry self-regulation to stronger government-led inspections and verification, and to consider tougher penalties for violations.

zh.headline: 政府周四公布宏福苑火警報告並提出圍標刑事化改革
zh.dek: 消息指行政長官李家超周四記者會公布獨立委員會調查結果，並闡述把樓宇維修圍標刑事化等措施。
body: 政府消息指，獨立委員會就去年11月大埔宏福苑火警的調查報告，預計周四公布。這場火警造成168人死亡。
消息人士表示，行政長官李家超周四將聯同主要官員舉行記者會，闡述一系列改革，包括立法把樓宇維修工程的圍標行為刑事化。周五另有簡報會詳細說明措施。
當局計劃成立由政務司司長領導的督導委員會，跟進報告建議及相關法例修訂。政府亦將提出修訂《建築物條例》，由業界自律轉為政府主導的加強查核及巡查，並研究提高違規罰則。
